thread:
maria: Heads-up — we found a partial credential spill in a partner ingestion bucket last night. not a full key leak but plaintext snippets referencing vault paths. starting a scoped cleanup and audit enrichment.

nate: can you paste the blob/line that triggered it? need to confirm if any wrapped ciphertext was exposed or just metadata.

maria: pasted minimal snippet: `s3://partner-uploads/2026-03-22/meta.json` -> contains `vault://kv-v2/projects/alpha/secret_id: lease=abcd1234` (no raw secret values).

sophia: that lease id is still valid in Vault. first priority: revoke that lease and ensure consumer tokens are evicted. i'll run `vault lease revoke abcd1234` unless someone objects.

maria: go for it. but before revoke, we should snapshot audit logs and create an enriched view that links the leak artifact -> vault path -> lease -> service account.

sec-oncall: agree. plan: 1) snapshot audit logs for the last 48h (vault + s3 access logs) 2) enrich logs with KMS envelope metadata where available 3) revoke lease 4) rotate any impacted wrapping keys if ciphertext exposure found 5) coordinate partner notification. any timing constraints?

nate: i can run the audit snapshot and join logs. command i'll use: `gsutil cp gs://infra-logs/vault-audit/2026-03-22/*.log ./tmp && python tools/log-enrich.py --map-kms --map-lease`

sophia: thanks. note that `log-enrich.py` will call KMS metadata endpoints — ensure it runs from a node with vault-readonly role, not with admin creds. i'm assigning a short-lived role for this job.

maria: tagging opsbot to create the ephemeral role: @opsbot please create ephemeral role `log-enrich-reader` for 1 hour scoped to vault-audit-read and kms-metadata-read.

opsbot: role created -> `log-enrich-reader`, ttl=3600s. creds posted to secure channel. :lock:

sec-oncall: after log snapshot: i'll correlate the s3 object who/which IP uploaded the file. nate can you push the enriched logs to `s3://sec-incident/4212349876/` once done? mark files as read-only.

nate: upload complete. files: `enriched_vault_audit.json.gz`, `s3_access_map.csv`. pushed with server-side-encryption=kms.

sophia: i've revoked lease abcd1234. output below: ```
Revoked lease abcd1234: success (revoked_tokens: 1, orphaned: 0)
```

maria: nice. next — evaluate if any KV v2 versioned values have been read by that lease or if it was only a metadata pointer. nate, can you run the KV audit query for path `projects/alpha` and filter by accessor ID tied to that lease?

nate: running: `vault audit search --path=kv/data/projects/alpha --accessor=XXXX` -> so far, only access events were `sys/lookup` and `metadata/get`. no plaintext values returned.

sec-oncall: good sign. still — we should rotate wrapping key for partner ingress to be safe. we'll do a rewrap (kms re-encrypt) of manifests keyed by `partners/ingest/key1` and schedule a non-blocking rotate window tonight at 02:30 UTC.

sophia: rewrap plan: stage: create new kek, re-encrypt wrapped blobs, publish new ciphertexts, then rotate alias. we should avoid re-encrypting large archives during business hours. i'll draft the runbook.

maria: also need RBAC check: partner service account `svc-partner-ingest` currently has `vault-kv-read` on `projects/alpha/*`. we should scope that down to `projects/alpha/ingest/*` and apply a deny for metadata endpoints for external service accts. nate, can you open the PR for the policy change?

nate: will do. PR: `github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/5042` — includes policy diff and smoke test. i will coordinate with sophia for rollout phases (canary -> ramp).

sec-oncall: rollout guidance: 1) canary to `svc-partner-ingest` in staging 2) run smoke reads for 15m 3) batch rollout to production with 5m pause between buckets 4) monitor vault audit for `denied` spikes 5) auto-rollback if error rate > 3% for 15m.

maria: for compliance, we need retention labels on the enriched audit bundle (PII, partner-data flagged). nate, add metadata tags: `incident=partner-20260322`, `retention=90d`, `owner=eng-security`.

nate: tags added. also added a short summary file `README.incident` with scope and contact.

sophia: quick question — do we need to rotate our KMS Customer Managed Key (CMK) used for s3 SSE-KMS? rotating it will re-encrypt many objects and could be heavy. alternative: create a new CMK and start using it for new objects + rewrap small set only. thoughts?

sec-oncall: prefer new CMK + rewrap only the artifacts that are directly linked to the incident (the partner objects + enriched bundles). broader CMK rotation can be scheduled separately. minimize blast.

maria: agree. let's capture that decision in the runbook and tag for a deferred CMK rotation ticket.

opsbot: incident ticket created -> INC-2026-03122 (priority P2). assignees: maria, sophia, nate, sec-oncall.

maria: final items: partner notification draft (legal reviewed) ready for approval; scheduled a short postmortem sync tomorrow 10:00 PT. if nobody has objections, i'll send the notify and start the canary policy change tonight.

nate: no objections from me.

sophia: approved.

deploy-bot: scheduled job `vault-policy-rollout/5042` -> starts 2026-03-23T02:30:00Z.

sec-oncall: closing loop: everything is staged, audit snapshot saved, lease revoked, limited rewrap plan approved, RBAC PR open and scheduled. postmortem will have timeline + action items. thanks all. :white_check_mark:

maria: thanks team. followups in INC-2026-03122 and PR 5042.

opsbot: archive note -> incident artifacts retained in `s3://sec-incident/4212349876/` for 90d.
